name: Architecture

subjectOf.text: A key design goal is a minimal and robust architecture, because minimality is what permits later construction of more complex automated validation logic and machine expert validators.
subjectOf.abstract: A key design goal of Semada is to create a minimal and robust architecture that allows for creating much more complex and automated validation logic, as well as machine expert validators.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900

subjectOf.text: Rather than repeating the same task across many workers to reach quality, the architecture verifies quality directly by examining and validating individual worker task performance through reputation verification.
subjectOf.abstract: Instead of repeating work on given tasks to attain high quality work products for micro tasks, Semada uses an architecture of reputation verification that examines micro worker task performance and verifies the validity and quality of the work.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: micro tasks routed through the reputation verification architecture

subjectOf.text: Probabilistic language models hallucinate because they are trained to predict statistically likely token sequences rather than to verify propositional truth, so the error is intrinsic to the substrate: plausibility and truth are orthogonal properties in high dimensional token space.
subjectOf.abstract: Probabilistic large language models hallucinate because they are trained to predict statistically likely token sequences, not to verify propositional truth.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Collapse of Scarcity Economics (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6421319

subjectOf.text: Hybrid neuro symbolic architectures structurally shrink the hallucination surface because the probabilistic layer generates candidate outputs while a symbolic layer filters, validates, and rejects any output violating formally specified rules, known ontological relations, or deductively verifiable constraints.
subjectOf.abstract: The probabilistic layer generates candidate outputs; the symbolic layer filters, validates, and rejects any output that violates formally specified rules, known ontological relations, or deductively verifiable constraints.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Collapse of Scarcity Economics (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6421319
scope_conditions: demonstrated in retrieval augmented generation and formal verification pipelines for code generation

subjectOf.text: The possibility loop is generatively open: each completed cycle leaves the system with a strictly enlarged action space, because a successful proposal adds a job specification, tag, or template that did not previously exist.
subjectOf.abstract: The possibility loop, in contrast, is generatively open in the sense that each completed cycle leaves the system with a strictly enlarged action space.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Possibility Loops An Operational Architecture for Computative Economics in Agent Coordination Systems (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6655138
scope_conditions: cycles that complete with a validated proposal

subjectOf.text: The architecture shows that the author arranged not to read the outcome early and that specified later adjustments would be detectable, and it does not show that the filter works or prove that the outcome was never read.
subjectOf.abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518
scope_conditions: Concerns the sealing and audit architecture of Section VI.
The negative half is the author's own statement of what the architecture cannot establish.
